prompt.context: Your client is Hotel Co., an international hotel corporation that owns and operates 2,700 hotels worldwide, as well as a separate timeshare business with 75 properties worldwide. Their hotel rooms are typically sold on a per night basis, whereas their timeshare properties are sold more like traditional homes via a mortgage which in turn gives the buyer the right to stay at a timeshare property for a set period of time each year. The CEO of Hotel Co. has approached you and has asked for guidance on whether or not they should spinoff their timeshare business into a separate stand-alone entity called Timeshare Co. Hotel Co. only uses a five-year timeframe for all financial decisions. If spun off and taken public, 20% of the IPO proceeds would be paid back to Hotel Co.; the remainder would go to Timeshare Co. and the underwriters. Hotel Co.'s bankers think they can sell 10 million shares at $220 each.
prompt.question: Should Hotel Co. spin off its timeshare business into a separate stand-alone public entity called Timeshare Co.? Hotel Co. wants to weigh the financial impact, risk, and strategic outlook.

clarifying_info.q: What criteria should we use to evaluate the spinoff?
clarifying_info.a: Hotel Co. wants to weigh the financial impact, risk, and strategic outlook. They use a five-year timeframe for all financial decisions.

clarifying_info.q: What are the IPO terms if Timeshare Co. is spun off?
clarifying_info.a: Hotel Co.'s bankers think they can sell 10 million shares at $220 each. 20% of the IPO proceeds go back to Hotel Co.; the remainder goes to Timeshare Co. and the underwriters.

clarifying_info.q: Does Hotel Co. currently cross-sell timeshares to hotel customers?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, there is cross-selling between the two businesses, though the exact volume is not specified upfront.

exhibits.title: Timeshare Co. Historic and Projected Profits
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing Timeshare Co. annual profits in millions (bar chart, left axis) alongside US Home Sales year-over-year percentage change (line chart, right axis) from 2007 through 2015, with 2011-2015 marked as projections.
exhibits.data: 2007: profit ~$200M, home sales ~+5%; 2008: profit ~-$200M, home sales ~-20%; years 2011*-2015* are projected; axes range from -$250M to +$250M (profit) and -25% to +25% (home sales %)

exhibits.title: Mortgage Default Expectations
exhibits.shows: A table listing annual mortgage default rates from 2007 to 2015, with 2011-2015 marked as projections (asterisked).

exhibits.title: Mortgage Portfolio's Contribution to Profits
exhibits.shows: A table listing the portion of Timeshare Co.'s total profits attributable to its mortgage portfolio, by year from 2007 to 2015, with 2011-2015 as projections.

framework: Financial impact: Compare 5-year projected profits of Timeshare Co. if kept in-house vs. one-time IPO proceeds Hotel Co. would receive if spun off
Risk assessment: Evaluate variability of Timeshare Co. revenues, particularly mortgage default rate exposure and its share of total profits
Strategic outlook: Examine cross-selling synergies between hotels and timeshares, brand implications, management focus, and alternative risk-mitigation options
Recommendation: Weigh financial near-equivalence against risk reduction benefit and strategic fit

questions.prompt: What is the financial impact of spinning off Timeshare Co.? Calculate both the IPO proceeds Hotel Co. would receive and the 5-year projected profits if Timeshare Co. is kept in-house.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 1 to read off or estimate the 5-year projected profits (2011-2015). The key insight is that US home sales are a good proxy for Timeshare Co. revenues. Candidate should also compute the IPO proceeds using the given share price and quantity, then apply the 20% split. The two figures are very close, making this a nuanced financial call.

math.setup: IPO proceeds to Hotel Co. = 10M shares x $220/share x 20%. 5-year projected profits = sum of annual projections from Exhibit 1 for 2011-2015.
math.answer: IPO proceeds to Hotel Co. = $440M vs. 5-year projected profits retained = $450M. Financially nearly identical; the $10M difference barely favors keeping Timeshare Co. in-house.

questions.prompt: What is the risk profile of Timeshare Co.'s business, and how does that affect the spinoff decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 2 to note that mortgage default rates spiked dramatically in 2008-2009 and appear to have settled at a structurally higher 'new normal' around 4.5%, never returning to pre-2008 levels (~1.5%). Exhibit 3 shows that mortgages consistently account for ~95% of Timeshare Co.'s profits, making the business extremely sensitive to default rate movements. The combination means the projected $450M in profits carries high variability, whereas the $440M IPO payout is largely certain. Candidate should also brainstorm risk-mitigation alternatives short of a full spinoff.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the risk implications of retaining the timeshare mortgage business, and what alternatives exist to reduce that risk without a full spinoff?

categories.name: Mortgage risk mitigation
ideas: Connect timeshare buyers with third-party mortgage companies and collect a finder's fee instead of carrying mortgages on Hotel Co.'s balance sheet
Purchase mortgage default insurance to reduce revenue volatility
Securitize the mortgage portfolio to transfer risk to capital markets

categories.name: Strategic considerations for spinoff decision
ideas: Examine cross-selling volume: how many timeshare buyers are also hotel customers, and how would that be maintained post-spinoff
Assess brand and management focus: does running a mortgage-heavy timeshare business distract Hotel Co.'s core hotel management
Evaluate whether a partial spinoff or minority stake sale achieves financial and risk goals while preserving synergies

categories.name: Market and timing factors
ideas: IPO market conditions may not always be as favorable as the bankers project
Projections assume a housing recovery; downside scenarios could make $450M unachievable
Regulatory differences between hotel operations and financial services (mortgage portfolios) may create compliance complexity for a combined entity

recommendation: Recommend proceeding with the spinoff of Timeshare Co.
The IPO proceeds ($440M) are nearly equivalent to the 5-year projected profits ($450M), but the projected profits carry substantial downside risk due to mortgage default rate volatility
Default rates appear to have reset to a structurally higher level (~4.5%) and are unlikely to return to pre-2008 lows (~1.5%), making the $450M projection optimistic
Receiving a largely certain $440M now is preferable to holding a volatile mortgage-heavy business that accounts for ~95% of its own profit through a single risk factor
risks: Cross-selling revenue between hotels and timeshares may decline post-spinoff, eroding Hotel Co.'s top line
IPO proceeds are dependent on market conditions; bankers' valuation of $220/share may not hold
Projected profits of $450M could exceed IPO proceeds if the housing market recovers faster than expected
next_steps: Quantify the cross-selling relationship: determine what share of timeshare buyers are hotel customers and model the revenue impact of losing that link
Explore contractual cross-selling agreements that could be maintained post-spinoff (e.g., referral fees, co-marketing deals)
Evaluate alternative risk-reduction mechanisms (mortgage default insurance, finder's fee model) as a fallback if the spinoff is not pursued
Confirm IPO valuation assumptions with multiple investment banks before proceeding
